articles.title: BBC reports from the front-line of an escalating war in Yemen
articles.summary: In rare access to Yemen's conflict zone the BBC travels to the front line with pro-government soldiers.
articles.body:
In rare access to Yemen's conflict zone, the BBC has travelled with government forces from Taiz through checkpoints to the line where the Houthi control ends and no man's land begins.

Saudi-backed pro-government forces are battling to push back Houthi fighters, who swept down the coast of the Red Sea earlier this month, taking control of a key shipping chokepoint and escalating Yemen's civil war.

From the front-line a drone is heard above, which a soldier accompanying the crew in south-western Yemen said is usually followed by an attack.

Within about 10 minutes, after the crew had driven away, the loud thuds of strikes followed, senior international investigations correspondent Nawal Al-Maghafi reports.

articles.title: Evento sobre migração da UFRR reúne pesquisadores da Noruega, Holanda, Portugal e França | G1
articles.standfirst: As inscrições são abertas ao público e a programação inclui visitas de campo a Pacaraima, na fronteira com a Venezuela, Bonfim, na divisa com a Guiana, e abrigos da Operação Acolhida, em Boa Vista.
articles.summary: As inscrições são abertas ao público e a programação inclui visitas de campo na fronteira com a Venezuela, na divisa com a Guiana, e abrigos da Operação Acolhida, em Boa Vista.
articles.body:
Universidade Federal de Roraima (UFRR), campus Paricarana, em Boa Vista, Roraima. — Foto: Reprodução/UFRR/Arquivo

Pesquisadores da Noruega, Holanda, Portugal e França discutem entre esta segunda-feira (28) e sexta-feira (2), as dinâmicas de migração, fronteiras e mobilidade humana em Roraima. As atividades fazem parte do evento internacional “(I)mobilidades e fronteiras”, realizado na Universidade Federal de Roraima (UFRR), em Boa Vista . As inscrições podem ser feitas no site oficial do evento.

A programação busca ampliar a produção e a troca de conhecimento sobre migração, fronteiras e mobilidade humana em Roraima. Além das atividades na universidade, os pesquisadores vão visitar as fronteiras do Brasil com a Venezuela e a Guiana e abrigos para migrantes em Boa Vista.

O evento reúne três encontros acadêmicos: o Seminário da Rede de Migração e Refúgio em Roraima, o VII Seminário Internacional do Programa de Pós-Graduação em Sociedade e Fronteiras (PPGSOF) e o Seminário em Comunicação Digital e Migração da UFRR.

As atividades discutem as mudanças nas migrações, nas fronteiras e nas diferentes formas de mobilidade humana . A programação reúne pesquisadores, estudantes, profissionais, representantes de instituições e integrantes de comunidades ligadas à migração.

Na terça-feira (29), os participantes visitam Pacaraima , cidade na fronteira do Brasil com a Venezuela. Na quarta (30), a programação inclui uma visita aos abrigos da Operação Acolhida , em Boa Vista.

Já na quinta-feira (1º), os pesquisadores seguem para Bonfim , na fronteira com a Guiana. As visitas ocorrem das 7h às 17h em Pacaraima, das 14h às 16h30 nos abrigos da Operação Acolhida e das 8h às 16h em Bonfim.

As atividades de campo permitem que os pesquisadores conheçam de perto as dinâmicas migratórias nas fronteiras e as políticas públicas voltadas aos migrantes.

A abertura acontece na segunda-feira (28) , às 18h, no auditório do PPGSOF, na UFRR. Em seguida, ocorre a mesa “A produção e a circulação da produção científica sobre as migrações internacionais” .

Na terça-feira (29) , às 18h, pesquisadores discutem fronteiras e interculturalidade no auditório do PPGSOF. Às 18h30, ocorre a roda de conversa “Migrações e comunicação digital na fronteira Brasil-Venezuela” , no auditório do Centro de Ciências Humanas (CCH).

A atividade é aberta a profissionais da imprensa, estudantes de Jornalismo e demais interessados, sem necessidade de inscrição.

Na quarta-feira (30) , a programação aborda as relações entre cultura, comunicação e mobilidade. Às 9h, no Salão Nobre da Reitoria, ocorre a mesa “Cultura como potência de transformação em contextos de (i)mobilidade” . Às 18h, pesquisadores discutem mobilidade, comunicação e tecnologias digitais no auditório do PPGSOF.

Na quinta-feira (1º) , a programação inclui discussões sobre migração forçada e a mobilidade de povos indígenas. As atividades começam às 18h, no auditório do PPGSOF, com a exibição do documentário “Mulheres e Migrações Forçadas no Rio de Janeiro: trajetórias dos corpos femininos, violência, xenofobia e resistências” . Em seguida, ocorre a mesa “Povos indígenas em mobilidade: fronteiras, direitos e desafios contemporâneos”.

O evento termina na sexta-feira (2) com a mesa “Cidades em contextos de Migrações” , às 18h, no auditório do PPGSOF. Também haverá apresentações de trabalhos na quinta e sexta-feira (1º e 2), das 14h às 18h, nas salas do CCH.

articles.title: Artista indígena, Posada conecta sons da Amazônia e da América Latina entre carimbó, cumbia, reggae e dancehall | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre vivências no Pará e raízes colombianas, Posada constrói uma música atravessada por ancestralidade e memória. Neste domingo (27), lança “Madrugada”, clipe inspirado em sua juventude em Belém.
articles.summary: Entre vivências no Pará e raízes colombianas, Posada constrói uma música atravessada por ancestralidade e memória. Neste domingo (27), lança “Madrugada”, clipe inspirado em sua juventude em Belém.
articles.body:
Artista indígena Posada — Foto: Igor de Paula

Pegar uma bicicleta e percorrer lugares da juventude pelas ruas de Belém : a Matinha, o reggae de São Brás, a Feira do Açaí, o rio Guamá e o Combu. É desse percurso afetivo e festivo que nasce o clipe de “Madrugada”, que a artista indígena Posada lança neste domingo (27), no YouTube .

Com raízes familiares colombianas e uma trajetória entre o Sul e o Norte do Brasil, a compositora, DJ e produtora faz da ancestralidade, da memória e do pertencimento pontos de partida para uma música que aproxima Amazônia e América Latina.

“Madrugada” é o primeiro clipe de “Flecha Envenenada” , álbum de estreia de Posada, lançado este ano. Nas oito faixas, carimbó, brega e côco convivem com reggae, dancehall, hip hop, bullerengue, cumbia, bolero e reggaeton, revelando uma formação musical construída entre diferentes territórios.

“Flecha Envenenada”, álbum de estreia de Posada, lançado este ano. — Foto: Divulgação

A ancestralidade indígena ocupa um lugar central nessa construção. Para Posada, falar de identidade também significa enfrentar os estereótipos sobre quem pode ser reconhecido como indígena.

“Eu sempre fui colocada num espaço em que as pessoas questionavam meu pertencimento étnico porque eu não correspondia a um estereótipo do que é ser indígena”, afirma.

Esse olhar também aparece na maneira como a artista pensa a presença indígena no mundo contemporâneo. Para ela, tradição e vida urbana não estão em lados opostos.

“Nós, povos indígenas, não somos povos do passado. Somos povos com uma tradição riquíssima, complexa, diversa e somos povos que também estão construindo presente e futuro.”

É em Belém que parte desse universo ganha agora imagens. Posada lança “Madrugada”, primeiro clipe de “Flecha Envenenada”. Dirigido por Guimarães Neto e realizado de forma independente, o vídeo recupera lugares e percursos ligados à adolescência da artista na capital paraense.

A narrativa começa na Matinha, onde estão referências familiares de Posada, e segue de bicicleta pela cidade. O trajeto passa por São Brás, Nando Vinil e Feira do Açaí antes de chegar às margens do rio Guamá e ao Combu. A bicicleta também vem dessa memória pessoal, como uma das formas usadas pela artista para circular por Belém durante a adolescência.

“É alguém que está retornando à cidade e quer viver esse dia”, conta Posada sobre a narrativa do vídeo.

Segunda faixa do álbum, “Madrugada” nasceu de um momento de renascimento pessoal e estabelece diálogos com reggae, dancehall, hip hop e música eletrônica. No clipe, a canção ganha uma geografia ligada às lembranças da artista, entre deslocamentos, encontros e lugares que fizeram parte de sua juventude.

Belém aparece por outro caminho em “Tenoné”, faixa que abre o disco em ritmo de côco. A composição nasceu das histórias sobre a infância da mãe de Posada no bairro de mesmo nome, entre noites, igarapés e brincadeiras que atravessaram gerações. Enquanto “Tenoné” parte de uma cidade transmitida pela memória familiar, “Madrugada” retorna à Belém vivida pela própria artista.

articles.title: Jovem desaparece na Praia de Atalaia após salvar namorada no Piauí | G1
articles.standfirst: O rapaz e a namorada tomavam banho de mar quando foram arrastados.
articles.summary: O jovem de 19 anos desapareceu na Praia de Atalaia após salvar a namorada de um afogamento e as buscas em Luís Correia serão retomadas nesta segunda-feira.
articles.body:
Um jovem de 19 anos desapareceu após um afogamento na Praia de Atalaia, em Luís Correia — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Um jovem de 19 anos desapareceu após um afogamento na Praia de Atalaia, em Luís Correia , no litoral do Piauí, neste domingo (27). Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o rapaz tomava banho de mar com a namorada quando os dois foram arrastados por uma forte onda para uma área de maior profundidade.

A jovem conseguiu sair da água após ser ajudada pelo namorado. Conforme relato dela aos militares, o rapaz a empurrou em direção à parte rasa da praia, mas acabou desaparecendo logo em seguida.

Quando as equipes de salva-vidas chegaram ao local, encontraram apenas a mulher. Ela foi resgatada sem ferimentos.

O jovem é natural de Teresina e havia viajado para o litoral piauiense acompanhado da namorada para passar o fim de semana.

Os trabalhos de busca foram encerrados no fim da tarde deste domingo e devem ser retomados na manhã de segunda-feira (28).

articles.title: Estudante da Ufac honra pai zelador e segue na medicina após luto | G1
articles.standfirst: Thainá Barros, de 21 anos, está na metade da graduação da Ufac e lida com a perda de Raimundo Carrilho, que incentivou nos estudos desde a infância e comemorou a aprovação da filha em 2023.
articles.summary: Thainá Barros, de 21 anos, está na metade da graduação da Ufac e lida com a perda de Raimundo Carrilho, que incentivou nos estudos desde criança e comemorou a aprovação da filha.
articles.body:
“Eu falo que ele é o grande amor da minha vida, porque sem ele eu não teria todo o apoio de poder chegar até aqui. Ele sempre foi um grande apoio, sempre acreditou em mim desde criança”.

Foi assim que Thainá Araújo Barros relembrou, em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, o pai de criação Raimundo Carrilho, enquanto tenta seguir a trajetória que os dois sonharam acompanhar juntos. Aos 21 anos, a estudante está no 6º período de Medicina da Universidade Federal do Acre (Ufac), na metade de uma formação que começou a construir ainda na infância. ( Assista acima )

Raimundo morreu no dia 2 deste mês, aos 80 anos, devido a complicações de um quadro de pneumonia. Em 2023, quando Thainá tinha 18 anos e acabava de conquistar uma vaga em Medicina, o zelador aposentado comemorou a aprovação e dizia que queria vê-la formada. O g1 contou a história de ambos na época.

Agora, ela precisa concluir os três anos que ainda faltam sem a presença física dele.

“A caminhada agora segue muito mais difícil pois não terei presencialmente ele para vivermos as alegrias que tanto almejamos, porém sei que dei muito orgulho para ele em vida, e até hoje tenho um amor incondicional por toda nossa trajetória. Não será fácil pois momentos difíceis virão, então pretendo ter forças pelo nosso sonho que ainda permanece vivo e respeito pela nossa história", destacou em entrevista ao g1.

Thainá ao lado dos avós, que tem como pais, em formatura no ensino méd — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Raimundo começou a trabalhar na roça aos oito anos e estudou apenas quatro. Já em Rio Branco , trabalhou como zelador do Mercado do bairro Seis de Agosto até se aposentar.

Embora não tenha tido oportunidades de estudo, fez do incentivo à educação da filha uma prioridade. Thainá contou que, desde criança, ele buscava livros para ela na biblioteca da escola e fazia o esforço que podia para ajudá-la nos estudos.

“Mesmo com a simplicidade dele em não ter tido oportunidades nos estudos quando era criança, ele não quis que fosse o mesmo comigo. A minha infância inteira ele sempre fez o esforço que podia para me auxiliar nos estudos. Acredito que, por desde criança reconhecer isso, foi o que me dava mais vontade para vencer na vida por meio da educação e valorizar o esforço dele por mim”, complementou.

Thainá Araújo, de 21 anos, está no 6º período do curso de Medicina da Ufac; g1 contou a história dela em 2023, quando foi aprovada — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Entre as lembranças dessa infância está um livro de astronomia que Thainá guarda até hoje. Ela contou que gostava de ciências e que, quando criança, pediu ao pai um livro sobre o assunto. Raimundo não conhecia o tema, mas foi atrás. Na época, com o dinheiro que tinha, comprou o exemplar por cerca de R$ 60.

Thainá leu a obra várias vezes e a conservou ao longo dos anos. Agora, o livro também se tornou uma forma de manter viva a memória do pai.

“Antes do falecimento, estávamos escolhendo sua roupa para nosso ensaio fotográfico, ele falava muito animado sobre esse dia. Eu compartilhei [o vídeo] para que as pessoas conhecessem mais a história dele, um homem de valor que tinha uma bondade genuína dentro do coração, pequeno em tamanho mas grande em alma, e que nossa história inspirasse também mais jovens da periferia de Rio Branco”, relembrou.

Thainá Araújo, de 21 anos, homenageia pai que morreu em Rio Branco durante ensaio de 'meio médica' da Ufac; na foto, Raimunda Carrinho (avó de Thainá e viúva de Raimundo) e Tinatana Benedita (mãe de Thainá) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Quando Thainá entrou na Medicina, sabia que a caminhada seria difícil. Ela estudou em escolas públicas, passou pelo Instituto Federal do Acre (Ifac), chegou a cursar Direito e depois conseguiu a vaga em Medicina pelo Sistema de Seleção Unificada (Sisu).

Para se preparar para o Enem, contou com um curso gratuito oferecido por estudantes de Medicina da Ufac. A rotina era puxada e exigia esforço dela e da família.

Raimundo fazia parte desse cotidiano. Thainá comentou que ele acordava cedo para acompanhá-la até a parada de ônibus e também a apoiava nos momentos mais difíceis.

“Ele foi de extrema importância para chegarmos até aqui. Apesar das pessoas terem um estereótipo sobre a medicina, esses anos foram bem difíceis pela quantidade de esforço que precisamos realizar para conseguirmos prosseguir no curso, principalmente na federal, e de termos que abrir mão de momentos em família em prol de um sonho”, disse.

Raimundo Carrilho morreu aos 80 anos em setembro deste ano — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Em 2023, ao comemorar a aprovação da filha, Raimundo contou ao g1 que fazia o possível para ajudá-la nos estudos. Três anos depois, Thainá está no meio do caminho que ele queria vê-la concluir.

Para a estudante, o sonho do pai ia além do diploma. Era também a possibilidade de mudar as condições de vida da família.

"Ele nunca impôs pra mim uma profissão ou faculdade específica. O que sempre quis foi que eu estudasse e conseguisse me formar no que eu quisesse, livre de pressão ou julgamentos próprios. Eu acredito que o principal sonho dele era a quebra de um ciclo da nossa desigualdade social , morar em um bairro onde não precisássemos ficar com medo de enchentes, uma habitação melhor e alimentação de qualidade, ter uma vida digna com o básico", comentou.

No vídeo em que homenageou o pai, Thainá lembrou que a dor da perda não muda o compromisso com a trajetória que os dois começaram ainda quando ela era criança. Agora, enquanto segue para os três anos finais da graduação, é esse o sonho que ela pretende continuar carregando consigo.

“Eu sei que hoje ele não está mais aqui. Meu coração está muito doído. Mas eu sei que lá de cima ele vai estar me acompanhando espiritualmente. E a gente vai chegar até a formatura daqui três anos ”, finalizou.

articles.title: Tentativa de feminicídio em Marília: homem invade casa da ex | G1
articles.standfirst: A vítima registrou o boletim de ocorrência na DDM, mas o suspeito fugiu. Mulher sofreu ferimentos na mão.
articles.summary: Suspeito de tentativa de feminicídio em Marília descumpriu medida protetiva, agrediu a ex-companheira e fugiu da polícia por uma área de mata.
articles.body:
Homem descumpre medida protetiva, invade casa da ex e tenta esfaqueá-la no pescoço em Marília — Foto: Gabriel Pelosi/TV TEM

Um homem de 30 anos descumpriu uma medida protetiva e invadiu a casa da ex-companheira, na Zona Norte de Marília (SP). O suspeito fez ameaças contra a vítima, a agrediu e tentou esfaqueá-la no pescoço.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, registrado na sexta-feira (25), a mulher ouviu barulhos no quintal e foi verificar. No local, encontrou o ex-companheiro, que havia pulado o muro.

A vítima relatou que ele ameaçou tirar a própria vida e também disse que iria matá-la. Em seguida, ele a agrediu puxando o cabelo dela, apertando seu pescoço e a empurrou contra um armário. Na cozinha, o suspeito pegou uma faca para tentar esfaquear a mulher no pescoço. Ela se protegeu com a mão e sofreu cortes.

O homem se recusou a deixar o local e acabou dormindo em um dos quartos da casa. Na manhã seguinte, ao sair para uma entrevista de emprego, a mulher percebeu que o ex-companheiro continuava no imóvel.

Veja abaixo os vídeos mais acessados do g1:

Após o compromisso, ela tentou ligar para a residência para checar se ele ainda estava lá. Sem retorno, a vítima foi à Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Marília para registrar o boletim de ocorrência.

Os policiais foram imediatamente ao endereço, onde encontraram o portão aberto e precisaram arrombar a porta da sala para entrar.

Ao perceber a presença dos policiais, o suspeito pulou o muro dos fundos e fugiu em direção a uma área de mata nas proximidades. Foram realizadas buscas pela região, mas ele não foi localizado.

A mulher possui medidas protetivas de urgência expedidas pela 3ª Vara Criminal de Marília, que proíbem o ex-companheiro de se aproximar ou manter contato por qualquer meio.

O caso foi registrado como descumprimento de medida protetiva de urgência, ameaça, injúria, lesão corporal e tentativa de feminicídio no âmbito de violência doméstica e da Lei Maria da Penha.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro confirma presença no debate da Globo contra Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à presidência da República deu declaração após uma carreata em Goiânia. Debate acontece na próxima quinta-feira.
articles.summary: Candidato à presidência da República deu declaração após uma carreata em Goiânia. Debate acontece na próxima quinta-feira.
articles.body:
O candidato à presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) anunciou que participará do debate na Globo, que acontece na próxima quinta-feira (1°). A declaração foi dada após uma carreata neste domingo (27), em Goiânia .

Flávio afirmou que pretende ir ao debate para "desmascarar" o atual presidente e também candidato, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

'Vou no debate da Globo. Está confirmado. Ele que lute. Eu quero ir para lá debater com ele. Eu estou chamando o Lula para o debate: 'Lula, eu quero você no debate da Globo, vem debater comigo porque eu vou esfregar verdade na sua cara e vou mostrar que o meu projeto de Brasil é melhor que o seu'", disse Flávio.

Flávio garantiu que irá ao debate, mesmo que Lula desista. Ele também citou pontos que pretende questionar o atual presidente, como a crise no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

O debate da Globo pode ser o único em que Lula e Flávio participarão no 1° turno. A votação acontece no próximo domingo (4).

Flávio Bolsonaro durante evento em Goiânia, Goiás — Foto: Diomício Gomes/O Popular

Por meio de Medida Provisória, Lula anunciou na sexta-feira (25) a proibição total de apostas online . A vedação inclui jogos online e cassinos virtuais, como o "Jogo do Tigrinho".

🔎 As MPs são publicadas pelo governo federal e passam a valer com força de lei imediatamente, mas devem ser votadas pelo Congresso em até 120 dias. Se isso não acontecer, perdem a validade.

Durante seu discurso em Goiânia, Flávio disse que vai "provar que o Lula é o pai do tigrinho". Na sexta-feira (25), ele já havia criticado o presidente pela decisão de proibir, a nove dias da eleição, a operação das bets no Brasil.

A declaração foi dada em um vídeo de campanha postado nas redes sociais. Flávio disse que Lula agiu de forma oportunista e chamou a Medida Provisória de "estelionato eleitoral" e "solução fajuta".

Por sua vez, no sábado (26), Lula justificou que tomou “atitude muito drástica” porque as apostas viraram "desgraça na vida das pessoas pobres". A declaração foi dada após uma caminhada de campanha em São Paulo.

"Quem quiser ganhar dinheiro, que arrume um jeito honesto de ganhar. Não matando o povo pobre e endividando o povo pobre. Ninguém fica rico apostando em bet. Quem fica rico é o dono da bet, o povo fica cada vez mais pobre”, afirmou o petista.

articles.title: VÍDEO: elefante Sandro entra em lagoa pela 1ª vez no Santuário em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens divulgadas pelo santuário mostram o elefante, de 54 anos, se refrescando durante o banho. No entanto, movimentação do animal chamou atenção da equipe.
articles.summary: Imagens divulgadas pelo santuário mostram o elefante, de 54 anos, se refrescando durante o banho. No entanto, movimentação do animal chamou atenção da equipe.
articles.body:
O elefante Sandro , de 54 anos, entrou pela primeira vez na lagoa do Santuário de Elefantes Brasil, em Chapada dos Guimarães , a 65 km de Cuiabá, após chegar a Mato Grosso. Em um vídeo publicado neste domingo (27), ele aparece se refrescando coberto de lama, mas demonstrando esforço para sair da água. Segundo a equipe do santuário, o animal está abaixo do peso e apresenta a musculatura debilitada .

De acordo com a publicação, ele vinha demonstrando mais interesse pelo lamaçal e pela água dos bebedouros. Quando a equipe voltou a encontrá-lo, o elefante já havia se banhado e estava coberto de lama.

O santuário chamou atenção para a dificuldade de Sandro ao subir a pequena rampa de acesso à lagoa. Segundo a equipe, a rampa tem uma inclinação suave e, entre os elefantes que já viveram no local, nenhum precisou fazer tanto esforço para sair da água.

Apesar da dificuldade, a equipe considera o banho uma oportunidade para Sandro se movimentar com menos impacto sobre o corpo. Caminhar na água pode ajudá-lo a se exercitar, enquanto o contato com a água amolece os pés e os prepara para os cuidados que serão feitos pelos tratadores .

Na primeira semana de adaptação ao santuário, Sandro também passou a receber uma dieta reforçada . Além dos alimentos que já recebia no zoológico, os cuidadores incluíram outros itens na alimentação para ajudar na recuperação física e no ganho de força. Segundo o santuário, a dieta poderá ser ajustada após a avaliação dos dentes do elefante e conforme sua evolução.

Elefante Sandro explora o novo recinto no Santuário de Elefantes Brasil, em Chapada dos Guimarães (MT). — Foto: Victoria Oliveira/g1

Sandro chegou ao Santuário de Elefantes Brasil depois de percorrer aproximadamente 1,6 mil quilômetros entre Sorocaba, no interior de São Paulo, e Chapada dos Guimarães. A viagem começou na quarta-feira (16) e durou dois dias, com paradas para alimentação e acompanhamento veterinário. Antes de chegar ao santuário, o elefante passou por Campo Verde (MT), onde foi realizada uma avaliação das condições físicas.

Ao chegar ao destino, a caixa de transporte foi aberta e deixou o compartimento rapidamente e começou a explorar o novo recinto. A transferência para Mato Grosso marca uma mudança importante na vida do animal. No local, ele passa a ter acesso a uma área maior, com vegetação, árvores, terra e lago, onde poderá desenvolver gradualmente maior autonomia.

Sandro também se tornou o primeiro elefante macho a viver no Santuário , que já abrigava seis fêmeas. Apesar de dividir a propriedade com elas, o animal permanece em um espaço separado. O manejo permite que Sandro veja, sinta o cheiro e se comunique com as fêmeas por meio de vocalizações, mas sem contato físico direto.

O tratador Sergio Domingues e o elefante Sandro no zoo de Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Eric Mantuan / g1

Antes de chegar a Mato Grosso, Sandro passou a maior parte da vida em cativeiro. O elefante viveu durante um período em um circo e, posteriormente, foi levado para o Parque Zoológico Municipal Quinzinho de Barros, em Sorocaba. No zoológico paulista, ele viveu durante anos ao lado da elefanta Haisa. Após a morte da companheira, Sandro passou a viver sozinho.

Depois de mais de quatro décadas no zoológico, a transferência para o santuário abriu uma nova etapa na vida do animal. Embora já tenha convivido com outros elefantes anteriormente, Sandro agora está em um ambiente diferente, com a presença de outras fêmeas nas proximidades e uma área planejada para estimular comportamentos mais naturais.

A adaptação, no entanto, acontece de forma gradual. Além de acompanhar a interação de Sandro com o novo ambiente, a equipe monitora o peso, a musculatura, a alimentação e as condições de saúde para definir os próximos passos do manejo.

articles.title: O que fizeram candidatos ao governo de PE neste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira atividades de Ivan Moraes (PSOL), João Campos (PSB), Professora Camila (UP), Raquel Lyra (PSD) e Renan Hallais (Missão) e Victor Assis (PCO). Guilherme Fonseca (PSTU) não teve agenda.
articles.summary: Confira atividades de Ivan Moraes (PSOL), João Campos (PSB), Professora Camila (UP), Raquel Lyra (PSD) e Renan Hallais (Missão) e Victor Assis (PCO).
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco nas eleições 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

Seis candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco cumpriram compromissos de campanha neste domingo (27), a uma semana do primeiro turno das eleições, que ocorre no dia 4 de outubro. As agendas reuniram panfletagens, caminhadas, carreatas e atos políticos em cidades do Grande Recife , Agreste e Sertão do estado.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição Raquel Lyra ( PSD ) promoveu caminhadas no Sertão e Agreste do estado. Já o ex-prefeito do Recife João Campos ( PSB ) concentrou a agenda em cidades do Sertão, onde realizou mini-carreatas.

Veja como foram as agendas dos candidatos (por ordem alfabética):

Neste domingo, Ivan Moraes cumpriu agendas na cidade de Olinda . Às 10h, o ex-vereador do Recife participou de evento de toque para Ibejis no Terreiro de Xambá, no bairro de São Benedito. À tarde, com concentração às 16h, o candidato do PSOL fez caminhada pelos Quatro Cantos.

O ex-prefeito do Recife realizou realizou três mini carreatas no Sertão do estado durante sua agenda de campanha neste domingo (27). A primeira foi em Salgueiro, às 9h30, a segunda foi às 15h no município de Araripina, e a terceira foi às 18h, em Ouricuri.

A candidata da Unidade Popular (UP) realizou pela manhã panfletagem na Feira do Troca, no bairro de Prazeres, em Jaboatão dos Guararapes . Já à tarde, ela visitou apoiadores em suas casas nos bairros de Passarinho e do Curado, no Recife.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição iniciou sua agenda de campanha com uma caminhada em Pesqueira, no Agreste do Estado, com concentração às 14h. Já às 16h, ela fez uma segunda caminhada, mas desta vez na cidade de Arcoverde, no Sertão de Pernambuco. À noite, Raquel Lyra voltou ao Agreste, na cidade de São Bento do Una, para uma terceira caminhada.

O candidato do Missão realizou reunião de alinhamento com toda a equipe às 18h.

O candidato Victor Assis participou, às 11h, do ato nacional Rui Presidente, na Avenida Paulista , em São Paulo. À tarde, às 15h, esteve presente em confraternização com apoiadores e militantes do PCO no Centro Cultural Benjamin, também na capital paulista.

articles.body:
Deadly strike hits market in Yemen’s Taiz

A strike on a market in the Yemeni city of Taiz has killed at least seven people and wounded 40, according to Houthi authorities. Government sources claim Houthi fighters had set up a military camp nearby, but conflicting accounts and limited ground access make the strike and its intended target difficult to verify independently.

articles.title: Granizo no RS: Sobe 9,5 mil o número de pessoas afetadas e 2,2 mil casas destelhadas; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Balanço da Defesa Civil aponta que cidades de Santiago, na região central, e Alegrete, na fronteira oeste, foram as mais afetadas pelo temporal de sábado. Ninguém ficou ferido, conforme órgão.
articles.summary: Balanço da Defesa Civil aponta que cidades de Santiago, na região central, e Alegrete, na fronteira oeste, foram as mais afetadas pelo temporal de sábado. Ninguém ficou ferido, conforme órgão.
articles.body:
Balanço divulgado no final da tarde deste domingo pela Defesa Civil apresenta aumento nos estragos espalhados pelo RS em razão da forte chuva de granizo: 9,5 mil pessoas afetadas, 2,2 mil casas danificadas e um ferido.

Em Santiago , foram 5 mil pessoas afetadas. Em Alegrete, 2 mil moradores, incluindo 1 ferido e deixando 10 pessoas desabrigadas. Em Capão do Cipó, 820 pessoas foram afetadas, e Catuípe, 800 moradores.

Vídeos mostram a intensidade da precipitação em Santiago no sábado. Veja acima.

Em alguns pontos da cidade, o volume de granizo foi tão grande que o chão ficou praticamente branco , como se estivesse coberto por uma camada de gelo.

Forte chuva de granizo em Santiago, no RS — Foto: Imagens cedidas/ Bibiana Thones

Balanço da Defesa Civil divulgado na tarde deste domingo (27):

9.517 pessoas afetadas (5 mil pessoas em Santiago; 2 mil pessoas em Alegrete)

Nenhum óbito confirmado, em investigação ou desaparecido

2.2 mil casas danificadas (1 mil casas em Santiago; 700 em Alegrete)

A instabilidade começou a avançar sobre a Fronteira Oeste do Rio Grande do Sul na tarde deste sábado.

Em Barra do Quaraí , houve registro de chuva com granizo . Já em Uruguaiana , um temporal chegou à região no início da noite.

Os fenômenos ocorrem em meio aos alertas emitidos pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), pela Climatempo e pela Defesa Civil Estadual, que já apontavam risco de instabilidade entre esta sexta-feira (25) e a próxima segunda-feira (28) .

De acordo com os avisos meteorológicos, a mudança no tempo está associada à atuação de uma área de baixa pressão localizada entre o norte da Argentina e o Paraguai . Esse sistema favorece o transporte de ar quente e úmido em direção ao Rio Grande do Sul, criando condições para a formação de temporais.

Chegada de tempestade em Uruguaiana nesse sábado (26) — Foto: Pablo Gimenes/ RBS TV

No domingo (27) , a instabilidade ganha abrangência. A Defesa Civil alerta para ventos que podem superar 90 km/h e granizo grande na Campanha, Oeste, Missões, Noroeste, Norte e Centro. O calor segue intenso no Norte e Noroeste, alcançando 35 graus em Horizontina. No extremo sul, o clima é mais ameno, com mínima de 12 graus no Chuí.

A segunda-feira (28) mantém o tempo instável devido à organização de um novo sistema frontal. A Defesa Civil alerta que os acumulados totais de chuva entre sábado e segunda-feira podem passar de 200 milímetros na Campanha e no Oeste do estado. Apenas em 24 horas, os volumes podem superar 170 milímetros nestas regiões.

articles.title: Luva que traduz Libras é criada por alunos do Cefet em Araxá | G1
articles.standfirst: Dispositivo desenvolvido por alunos do Cefet, em Araxá, pode facilitar a comunicação entre pessoas surdas e ouvintes, além de contribuir para o ensino de Libras.
articles.summary: A luva que traduz Libras, criada no Cefet Araxá, usa sensores e inteligência para promover a acessibilidade e facilitar a comunicação de pessoas surdas.
articles.body:
Tecnologia desenvolvida no Cefet pode ajudar a tornar comunicação mais acessível para pessoas surdas — Foto: Foto/ Divulgação Cefet

Uma luva equipada com sensores capazes de identificar movimentos das mãos e reconhecer gestos que fazem parte da Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) está sendo desenvolvida por alunos do ensino técnico do Centro Federal de Educação Tecnológica (Cefet), em Araxá . A tecnologia pode ajudar a tornar a comunicação mais acessível para pessoas surdas.

Segundo o professor que coordena o projeto, Leandro Mattioli, o grupo trabalha no desenvolvimento do dispositivo há cerca de quatro meses, em continuidade a uma pesquisa iniciada no ano passado.

“Em 2025, nós começamos a desenvolver um sensor que conseguia estimar o posicionamento das mãos durante os gestos. Agora, aprimoramos esse sensor e acoplamos o dispositivo a uma luva para que os movimentos sejam capturados de forma mais precisa”, explicou o professor.

Na prática, os sensores instalados na luva trabalham em conjunto com uma câmera infravermelha. Os movimentos feitos pelo usuário são capturados e analisados por um programa de computador, que identifica os sinais e transforma o conteúdo em texto ou áudio.

Nos primeiros testes realizados com o protótipo, o sistema alcançou 92% de precisão no reconhecimento de sinais de Libras feitos por diferentes pessoas.

“O resultado é extremamente promissor e agora vamos continuar trabalhando para aperfeiçoar o sistema”, afirmou Leandro.

Luva tecnológica pode facilitar comunicação com pessoas surdas em Araxá — Foto: Cefet/\Divulgação

Quatro alunos do ensino técnico do Cefet Araxá participam diretamente do desenvolvimento do projeto. O dispositivo ainda está em fase de testes e não há previsão para que a versão final seja disponibilizada para comercialização.

Um dos desafios encontrados pelos estudantes foi ajustar os sensores para que os movimentos das mãos fossem captados com precisão, sem interferir na execução dos sinais.

“No início, tivemos dificuldade para ajustar os sensores, permitindo que eles capturassem os gestos de forma exata, sem interferir nos resultados. Algumas letras do alfabeto em Libras precisam de movimento, e o equipamento tem certa limitação: ele só consegue interpretar letras estáticas”, explicou o estudante Gregory Matsushita, de 17 anos.

Segundo ele, a equipe trabalha agora para ampliar as possibilidades do dispositivo e permitir o reconhecimento também de sinais que envolvem movimentos contínuos.

A expectativa dos estudantes é concluir o desenvolvimento da tecnologia nos próximos meses. Mais do que aprimorar o funcionamento do equipamento, o objetivo é criar uma ferramenta que possa aproximar pessoas surdas e ouvintes e facilitar a comunicação no dia a dia.

“Nosso objetivo é melhorar a comunicação entre pessoas surdas e pessoas que não são surdas. Com a tradução feita pelo equipamento, deficientes auditivos que se comunicam em Libras poderão conversar com quem não entende essa linguagem de forma simples, com acessibilidade e inclusão”, destacou o estudante Matheus Milagres, de 16 anos.

articles.title: Hurricane season is broken. Two oceans are historically out of whack
articles.summary: El Nino is just one reason for a wildly uneven hurricane season. The Atlantic is historically quiet, while the Pacific is a parade of powerful storms.
articles.body:
The 2026 hurricane season has been remarkable, from the potentially record-breaking calm in the Atlantic Ocean to the hyperactive eastern and central Pacific Ocean.

Only seven tropical storms have formed in the Atlantic, while 18 tropical storms and hurricanes have formed in the Pacific. In a normal year, the Atlantic and the eastern Pacific hurricane basins see similar activity, with 14 to 15 named storms, including seven to eight hurricanes by the time the season ends on Nov. 30. This year, the Atlantic hasn't yet produced a single hurricane, while the eastern Pacific has already produced eight.

What's interesting about this season is that a few of the storms that have occurred in the two basins originated in Africa and were influenced by the same powerful climate phenomenon, El Niño . But the results have been very different, with fierce hurricanes in the Pacific and unremarkable tropical storms in the Atlantic.

Meteorologists and climate scientists have closely watched the progression of these tropical waves and storms from their origins to their final destination using a fleet of satellites operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration . More than 60 years after satellites began helping observe hurricanes, they are still learning more about how and where tropical waves begin and how they develop and move. They watch as waves form in the Ethiopian mountains, over the Sahara or off the African coast, and then track them across the Atlantic and sometimes well into the Pacific.

This summer, there hasn't been a lot to see in the Atlantic. Tropical waves that do appear are being disrupted by shearing winds related to the El Niño. When Tropical Storm Gonzalo formed in the Atlantic on Sept. 25, it was only the season's seventh named storm, and it formed three weeks later than typical for the storm named with the letter "G" each season.

Don't look for Gonzalo to become a hurricane, either. It's expected to be yet another example of how hostile the Atlantic Ocean has been to tropical cyclones this year. One other storm also was active in the Atlantic on Sept. 25. Tropical Storm Fay was in the open ocean, while Gonzalo was moving through the Cape Verde Islands.

Meanwhile, the central and eastern Pacific has seen 18 named storms and could see two more by early October, according to the National Hurricane Center.

Conditions in both basins are at least partially linked to the "super El Niño," said Stacy Stewart, a former hurricane specialist at the National Hurricane Center, now retired and teaching meteorology courses at Embry Riddle-Aeronautical University.

However, while the relative calm in the Atlantic can be primarily attributed to El Niño, it's not the only thing keeping hurricane activity tamped down, Stewart told USA TODAY. A drought in Ethiopia has also contributed to the quiet Atlantic season, as have dry air and Saharan dust.

2026 hurricane season reaches peak period. See activity so far.

Three hurricanes can be seen across the Pacific Ocean in this satellite image: Nolo, Odalys and Polo. They are among 18 named storms in the central and eastern Pacific this year.

Residents across the Atlantic's hurricane basin may not be aware that many tropical waves originate over the Ethiopian Highlands, Stewart said.

The waves are among dozens that develop and move off Africa into the Atlantic Ocean each year, Kelly Núñez Ocasio, an assistant professor in the department of atmospheric sciences at Texas A&M University, told USA TODAY.

Most of the waves that move off the coast of western Africa never become tropical storms or hurricanes. But for the storms that do develop, waves that originate over the Ethiopian Highlands are the ones more likely to become hurricanes, Núñez Ocasio said.

That's in part because the Ethiopian mountains help form big storm clusters.

Some of the waves that form in Africa continue moving all the way across the extreme northern end of South America and emerge into the eastern North Pacific, where they can trigger the development of tropical cyclones there and in the Central Pacific, Stewart wrote in an email.

Both Fausto and Genevieve, two of the Pacific hurricanes this summer , developed from areas of disturbed weather that rolled off the hot, dry African continent near the island nation of Cape Verde, according to NOAA. The waves traveled westward, crossed Central America and eventually found favorable conditions over the eastern Pacific, where they strengthened into hurricanes.

The drought in Ethiopia meant a lack of the kind of thunderstorm activity needed to produce the big storm clusters and tropical waves that are "strong enough to survive the trek across the African Sahel region and resist shear conditions" over the Atlantic, Stewart said. "June and July 2026 brought some of the driest conditions on record, with rainfall deficits reaching 40% to 70% in northern, eastern, and central Ethiopia."

How quiet has this season been in the Atlantic?

"The last time we went this long without an Atlantic hurricane was in 1914," said Phil Klotzbach, a senior research scientist with the Department of Atmospheric Science at Colorado State University. "Of course, who knows what we really had for activity in 1914?"

The accumulated cyclone energy so far this season in the Atlantic is around nine, compared to a typical total by 88 in late September, according to Colorado State's running tally. That's the lowest since 1925, when storms were likely missed or underestimated, given the lack of aircraft reconnaissance and satellites, Klotzbach said.

"I really think the big story this year has been record high levels of vertical wind shear across the tropical Atlantic," Klotzbach said. "The constant shredding of any system trying to develop has been a common theme so far this year, and as Yogi Berra used to say, 'it's getting late early.' While we certainly can't rule out a late-season hurricane or two, this season is certainly shaping up to be one of (if not the) quietest seasons since 1950 (when reasonably reliable records began)."

The Pacific Ocean, on the other hand, has had an uncharacteristically busy season. In contrast to the Atlantic, the eastern Pacific season already has an accumulated cyclone energy total of 235, compared to the 108 more typical for this time of year. The El Niño has produced very warm water and low wind shear, the kind of conditions that allowed Hurricane Polo to rapidly intensify this week and hit sustained wind speeds of 180 mph.

That's also one reason why the Hawaiian Islands are having yet another encounter with the impacts of a passing hurricane or tropical storm, as Hurricane Nolo moves near the state on the last weekend in September. The Central Pacific has seen seven storms and hurricanes this season. Only seven other seasons since 1970 have had that much activity or more.

While no known hurricane has been designated in the Atlantic, some meteorologists suspect Tropical Storm Fay may have briefly hit hurricane strength on Sunday, Sept. 20. It wasn't visited by hurricane hunter reconnaissance flights, so forecasters didn't have an abundance of information.

The center was relying on satellite observations and estimates to make forecasts. Fay's peak winds in the hurricane center's advisories topped out at 70 mph, just below hurricane strength.

Could it have been a hurricane, however briefly? Only time will tell. Dan Brown, the hurricane center's operations division chief, told USA TODAY that the storm would get a thorough review during the preparation of the center's post-storm report in the coming weeks.

The center conducts a post-analysis of every tropical cyclone, and those analyses can result in changes to intensity and storm status. For example, Hurricane Michael in 2018 was upgraded from a Category 4 to a Category 5 after an analysis of its peak wind speeds. Brown said revisions can raise or lower intensities and adjust the time a system achieved tropical cyclone status or crossed a threshold from one classification or category to another.

Dinah Voyles Pulver, a national correspondent for USA TODAY, writes about violent weather, climate change and other news. Reach her at dpulver@usatoday.com .

articles.title: Afghanistan says 28 fighters killed, 32 captured after crossing from Pakistan
articles.summary: Afghanistan said on Sunday that its forces killed 28 fighters and captured 32 others, including alleged members of the Islamic State group said to have cross...
articles.body:
KABUL, Afghanistan (AP) — Afghanistan said on Sunday that its forces killed 28 fighters and captured 32 others, including alleged members of the Islamic State group said to have crossed from neighboring Pakistan.

Tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan have increased in recent days, with cross-border fighting and Pakistani airstrikes on Afghan territory adding to longstanding disputes over militant activity along their border.

Afghanistan's Defense Ministry said in a post on X that the fighters were killed or captured on Saturday in Kamdesh district in the northeastern province of Nuristan. It alleged that several IS-affiliated groups had been sent from Pakistan with the support of Pakistani authorities "with the aim of carrying out acts of subversion and creating insecurity."

Afghanistan does not recognize its frontier with Pakistan as an international border. The countries share a 2,611-kilometer (1,622-mile) boundary known as the Durand Line.

Pakistan rejects Afghanistan's accusations

Pakistan's Ministry of Information rejected the allegations as "frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth." In a post on X, it said Pakistan "categorically rejects" claims that its security forces or intelligence agencies were involved in clashes in Nuristan or elsewhere in Afghanistan. It also denied recruiting or training former Afghan security personnel or facilitating IS or other militants.

The ministry said Afghanistan had provided no evidence to support its allegations, including identities, documents, communications or forensic material. It dismissed a video circulating on social media as showing only a few unarmed people and described it as part of a "pre-planned video shoot" by Afghanistan's Taliban government.

Pakistan said the presence and activities of militant groups in Afghanistan had been documented in reports by the United Nations and other international organizations. It accused Kabul of trying to "manufacture a Pakistani connection" to obscure what it described as the continued presence of militants in Afghanistan.

Islamabad says its forces killed scores of militants

Meanwhile, Pakistan's military said Sunday that its forces had killed more than 71 militants during multiple operations in southwestern Balochistan province over the previous 96 hours. The military said the operations targeted hideouts of groups it refers to as Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan, terms used by Islamabad for Afghanistan-based Pakistani Taliban and members of the outlawed Baloch Liberation Army, or BLA.

Pakistan frequently accuses Afghanistan's Taliban government of allowing the Pakistani Taliban, formally known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, to operate from Afghan territory and carry out attacks inside Pakistan. The TTP is separate from Afghanistan's Taliban but is allied with it. Kabul denies providing the group a safe haven and has rejected Pakistan's accusations.

The latest hostilities followed Pakistani airstrikes Monday on sites in eastern Afghanistan that Pakistan described as militant hideouts. Pakistan said the strikes killed 28 militants , while Afghan authorities said three civilians were killed, a toll confirmed by the United Nations.

The Afghan Defense Ministry said most of those involved in the alleged Nuristan plot were former members of Afghanistan's military who served under the previous government, which was ousted when the Taliban returned to power in August 2021.

"According to available information, Pakistani intelligence agencies had brought them to Pakistan under the promise that arrangements would be made for them to obtain asylum in foreign countries and receive high salaries," the ministry said.

It alleged that the men were instead taken to camps established by Pakistan's military and intelligence agencies, given brief military training and sent back into Afghanistan to create insecurity in parts of Nuristan, which borders Pakistan's northern Chitral district.

The ministry called on "all young people and former military personnel who have been deceived by Pakistani intelligence agencies" not to become further victims of what it described as enemy conspiracies.

articles.title: RNC rips Beshear's 'woke trans record' over veto of Kentucky girls' sports bill
articles.summary: Kentucky Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear defended his veto of a transgender athletes ban, saying his party doesn't "throw anybody under the bus."
articles.body: Kentucky Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear defended his record on transgender issues Sunday during an appearance on CNN's "State of the Union," saying his party does not "throw anybody under the bus," as host Jake Tapper pressed him over his veto of a bill barring transgender students from girls' and women's sports. Tapper confronted Beshear about his 2022 veto of Kentucky's Senate Bill 83, which prohibited male students from participating on girls' athletic teams from sixth grade through college. The Republican-controlled legislature later overrode Beshear's veto. The governor pointed to what he described as Kentucky's lone transgender athlete at the time before defending his broader approach. FEMALE ATHLETES, WOMEN'S SPORTS ADVOCATES SPEAK ON CAPITOL HILL AS TRANS ATHLETE ISSUE HOVERS OVER MIDTERMS "Here's my take. We don't throw anybody under the bus," Beshear said, "That is not the party that we are. We start as a party of compassion and empathy. And I tell you what. If we want to ruin sports, put government in charge of them." RNC National Press Secretary Natalie Baldassarre ripped Beshear's record in an exclusive statement to Fox News Digital, accusing the potential 2028 presidential contender of putting transgender policies ahead of female athletes. "Democrats claim to be the party of women," she said. "But they can't define what a woman is and have no issues when men expose themselves in locker rooms or take over women’s sports. Andy Beshear can pretend he’s for fairness, but his woke trans record shows he traded girls' safety for applause from men in dresses." DEMOCRAT POLITICIANS ARE BETRAYING THEIR OWN VOTERS ON TRANS SPORTS ISSUE Beshear told Tapper that he believed athletic competition should be fair but rejected abandoning transgender Americans as Democrats face political attacks over the issue. "Sports need to be fair, and there should be no unfair advantage," Beshear said. "But, in Kentucky, we already had rules in place with our Kentucky High School Athletic Association that prevented any of the things that you saw ultimately in colleges or the rest." Kentucky legislative records show the 2022 legislation, Senate Bill 83, known as the "Save Women's Sports Act," dealt with athletics and did not include restrictions on transgender medical treatments for minors. The measure required girls' and women's athletic teams to be based on biological sex and prohibited male students from participating in them. SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS Those healthcare and school-facility provisions instead appeared in Senate Bill 150, a separate measure Beshear vetoed in 2023. The legislation restricted transgender medical treatments for minors and required school policies limiting students from using restrooms, locker rooms or showers reserved for the opposite biological sex. Republican lawmakers also overrode that veto. Beshear had argued in his 2022 veto message that existing Kentucky High School Athletic Association rules were sufficient to protect competitive fairness. The rules at the time generally required athletes to participate according to the sex listed on their birth certificate, while providing a pathway for transgender athletes who met specified medical requirements. His campaign said in 2023 that his opposition was based on multiple provisions in the legislation and was not specifically about its prohibition on sex-change surgeries for minors. articles.title: South Korea, Ukraine relations sour over North Korean POW transfer
articles.summary: South Korea’s presidential office criticised Ukraine for denying POW nondisclosure agreement.
articles.body:
The South Korean president’s office has demanded ⁠an official explanation and ⁠apology from Ukraine, accusing Kyiv of disclosing the transfer ‌of North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to South Korea, despite a prior agreement ⁠to keep the ⁠matter confidential.

The presidential office said ⁠on Sunday that Ukraine’s subsequent denial that ⁠any confidentiality ⁠agreement existed was false had damaged ‌trust and caused serious disruptions between the two governments.

Last week, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) that his country transferred two North Korean POWs to South Korea.

South Korean media reported that the president’s office expressed “strong regret” over Ukraine’s disregard for the nondisclosure agreement it had with Seoul regarding the two POWs.

The office said the nondisclosure agreement aimed to safeguard the soldiers from dangers they could face if their transfer were to be disclosed, in accordance with international law and humanitarian principles.

According to Yonhap, a South Korean media outlet, the Ukrainian presidential office said it had disclosed the transfer of the POWs without extensive details on the process, claiming that it would have been strange to keep the entire transfer a secret. Ukrainian media outlets reported a Ukrainian presidential source as denying the existence of a confidentiality agreement with Seoul, Yonhap said.

Seong Ghi-hong, South Korea’s senior presidential secretary for public relations, said the government was considering additional measures over the issue, if necessary, Yonhap added.

Ukrainian forces captured the two North Korean soldiers in Russia’s Kursk region in January 2025.

Mounting evidence, including from intelligence ⁠reports and testimonies of defectors, has indicated that North Korean soldiers resorted to self-detonation or other forms of suicide rather than be captured.

In his UN address, Zelenskyy said, “These guys are not easy to capture alive.” He added, “One of them, when he realised he was going to be taken prisoner, tried to kill himself. And he was shocked that fate did not let him die.”

South Korean media reported that the two captured soldiers had expressed their desire to defect to South Korea.

The issue of North Korean prisoners of war was a key topic during the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkiye, where Lee met Zelenskyy in July.

Senior presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung stated afterwards that both leaders agreed to resolve the status of North Korean POWs in accordance with international law. This built on a prior agreement reached during the South Korea-Ukraine foreign ministers’ meeting in March, where both nations pledged to cooperate on the POW issue.

According to South Korean intelligence, North Korea is estimated to have deployed approximately 14,000-15,000 soldiers to support Russia’s efforts in its war with Ukraine since 2024, primarily in the Kursk border region . South Korean, Ukrainian and Western officials said they suffered heavy casualties, with more than 6,000 North Korean soldiers killed in the fighting.

The transfer comes as South Korea has backed efforts to revive dialogue with North Korea, while United States President Donald Trump has renewed his willingness to engage with Pyongyang.

articles.title: Weston-super-Mare cardboard pier sculpture falls after wind hits
articles.summary: The six-storey-high art installation was subject to "monumental jumping and squashing" after it fell.
articles.body:
A giant cardboard model tower has fallen victim to strong sea winds.

The six-storey-high art installation, inspired by Weston-Super-Mare's crumbling Birnbeck Pier, was put up in the Prince Consort Gardens on Saturday by local people under the instruction of artist Olivier Grossetête.

The tower began to lean at about 07:00 BST on Sunday and had completely fallen down by 11:00, project leaders said.

Bosses ensured the site was safe so people could watch it happen. When the 20m (66ft) structure finally fell, about 300 members of the community in the park helped with some "monumental jumping and squashing" to prepare it for transportation and its recycling, they added.

articles.title: At least 12 dead and dozens missing after a vessel capsizes in DRC
articles.summary: This incident comes only two days after at least 41 people died in another boat capsizing in DRC.
articles.body:
A vessel carrying fish traders has capsized in Lake Kivu in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), killing at least 12 people with dozens still missing, authorities said.

The vessel was carrying more than 50 people on Saturday night near Idjwi Island in South Kivu province, said Félix Habiragi, chief of the village of Kisheke near the scene.

He said the cause of the accident was not immediately clear and about 15 people were rescued.

The vessel was transporting fish traders and goods from Bwina on Idjwi Island to Boza, according to local administrator, Muhindo Ntambuka Pascal. Videos that appear to be from the scene showed villagers and other passengers pulling bodies from the lake.

Boat accidents are common in the DRC, as rivers and lakes are a major means of transport for over 100 million people. Vessels are often overloaded with goods and passengers, many of whom frequently travel without life jackets.

“The authorities had, in particular, begun requiring passengers to wear life jackets. Today, however, many people continue to travel without them,” said Dorcelle Bagazane, a civil society member in Idjwi.

Earlier this week, at least 41 people died and 49 were rescued when a boat capsized on Lake Tanganyika in the DRC. It was reportedly carrying about 100 people and cargo when it capsized near the Congolese village of Mapera.

articles.title: Bill Gates says AI without regulation is ‘completely irresponsible’
articles.summary: The billionaire cofounder of Microsoft says, without restrictions, AI could ‘cause a billion deaths’.
articles.body:
Not requiring AI to have safeguards and be subject to outside monitoring is “completely irresponsible” and could lead to global harm to humanity, said tech mogul Bill Gates , in a series of media appearances where the philanthropist weighed in on global discussions concerning how to regulate the technology.

“You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion of what safeguards and monitoring looks like,” Gates said in an interview with NBC’s Meet the Press, parts of which aired on Sunday.

Gates warned that the technology was “certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths.” Ensuring that did not happen, he said, could be a more difficult task than other existential threats, such as slowing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

The tech pioneer turned philanthropist said he was willing to speak with US President Donald Trump to convey his concerns directly and disagreed with his characterisation of recent warnings over the danger AI posed as a “hoax”.

“I hope that, given ⁠⁠my life’s work in the field, my saying how unique and different this is and how concerned I am will add to what he’s hearing from other people,” Gates said in the interview.

In recent weeks, the heads of leading AI companies have said publicly that their industry needs frameworks and guardrails to ensure the technology does not outpace human oversight, spin out of control and prove to be catastrophic for the world.

“If managed poorly, I even believe AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Dario Amodei, the chief executive officer of Anthropic, the company behind Claude, told members of the United Nations Security Council last week.

But Trump and senior officials in his administration have baulked at imposing regulations on the multi-trillion-dollar industry, which they say is part of a race between the US and China.

On Saturday, the day after meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping to discuss AI, Trump repeated his scepticism of the warnings and said he would not regulate the industry. He compared the apocalyptic warnings to other issues he is dismissive of, such as climate change and Russian interference in US elections. “It’s just like, everybody’s going to be dead, you’re all supposed to be dead now because of global warming. It’s like Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. All of these different hoaxes,” Trump said.

Gates told CNN that the kind of safeguards needed for AI development would not harm the industry.

“The amount of slowing down is not going to be that dramatic,” he said. “To have a monitoring or policing layer that says, is this being used for a cyberattack, is this being used for bio-terrorism, that can be done.”

The 70-year-old co-founded the software company Microsoft in 1975 and ran it during an era of widespread consumer adoption of personal computers and later the internet. He became the richest person in the world in 1995, and retained that spot throughout much of the next two decades, before giving much of his wealth away for philanthropic causes and being replaced by a new generation of tech moguls, including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg.

Earlier this month, his philanthropy, the Gates Foundation, said it was committing $1bn to expand AI access in the developing world.

articles.title: More than 50 Palestine Action support rally protesters arrested
articles.summary: More than 250 protesters sat outside Labour's party conference in Liverpool to support the banned group.
articles.body:
More than 50 demonstrators have been arrested outside the Labour Party conference in Liverpool during a protest in support of the banned Palestine Action group, police have said.

More than 250 protesters sat outside the conference centre earlier, many holding home-made banners which read: "I support Palestine Action".

Scores of police officers stood by before moving in to start making arrests, warning protesters they were illegally holding signs supporting a proscribed organisation.

After asking them if they were going to continue to do so, officers led some of the protesters away, telling them they had been arrested under the Terrorism Act.

Merseyside Police said more than 50 people had so far been detained at the Defend Our Juries event and that officers were in the process of making arrests on suspicion of wearing/carrying an article supporting a proscribed organisation.

A force spokesperson said it respected everyone's rights to protest lawfully while also aiming to keep the peace and ensure public safety.

The force said it made "detailed and co-ordinated plans ahead of such events to ensure it can apply this consistently, fairly and proportionately".

The spokesperson said not everyone present at the protest had been committing a criminal offence.

The arrests were criticised by Amnesty International, which called them a "shameful attack on freedom of speech".

One of those detained was human rights barrister Margaret Owen, 94.

A spokesperson for Defend Our Juries said: "We had hoped the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, would do the sensible thing and bin the ban on Palestine Action given the weight of public pressure to do so and the escalating amount of resources required in enforcing it.

"Continuing the charade of the proscription of Palestine Action is illogical, unsustainable and immoral."

Demonstrators in Liverpool cheered every time someone was carried away by police.

Kerry Moscogiuri, chief executive of Amnesty International UK, said: "Protesting is one of the most effective tools we have to make our leaders listen to us, but we have seen consecutive governments crack down on our right to do it.

"The arrests of grandparents, teenagers and everyone in between for holding placards outside the Labour Party conference are a truly shameful attack on freedom of speech.

"The new prime minister can reform our laws so that communities are protected in coming together and demonstrating on the issues they care about. Will he do so?"

The court said it had given the group's co-founder permission to appeal the ban, which came into force in July 2025.

In a statement issued shortly afterwards, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the government would "robustly defend this appeal".

The Home Office has repeatedly said that the ban of the group has nothing to do with protest in support of Palestinian causes - and was necessary because it was causing significant criminal damage to legitimate businesses.

Both the High Court and the Court of Appeal have ruled that Palestine Action's activities include criminal acts - although they were divided on whether those incidents justified turning to terrorism laws.

BBC News has asked the Ministry of Justice to comment.

articles.title: Embattled Serbian president resigns, paving way for early elections
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vučić's administration has been dogged by prolonged protests over allegations of corruption.
articles.body:
Serbia's president has resigned after more than a year of student-led protests and growing public discontent over allegations of government corruption.

Aleksandar Vučić said his administration had preserved peace and stability during his nine-year tenure as he addressed supporters outside the presidential building in the capital, Belgrade.

He had already announced his intention to resign in June and is currently standing to be his party's candidate for prime minister in the upcoming parliamentary elections. Vučić cannot run for a third presidential term under Serbia's constitution.

The pro-Russian populist's administration has been dogged by anger over alleged corner-cutting.

It was the collapse of the Novi Sad railway station's roof , killing 16 people, that first galvanised anger towards the government in 2024.

Protests involving a wide range of citizens - from students and teachers to workers and farmers - followed.

Demonstrators believed that the disaster reflected more than a decade of governing by the Progressive Party of Vucic, who closely associated himself with the station's renovation, which was supposed to be a symbol of Serbia's progress.

A series of resignations of those under the embattled president failed to placate the protesters, who continued to demonstrate throughout this summer, turning to unrest following accusations of police brutality .

Vučić's presidency was due to expire next year. Under Serbia's constitution, presidential elections must be held no more than three months after his resignation.

This means Serbians will go to the polls twice before the end of the year.

Vučić said the presidential election will take place more than a month after the snap parliamentary election in late October, itself called in response to the protests, which had added calls for a vote to their list of demands.

He had earlier announced that he planned to run in that election as Progressive Party's leader, leaving the possibility he could retain a position at the top of Serbian politics.

Parliamentary speaker Ana Brnabić, also a Progressive Party member, will assume the role of interim president until a new one is elected.

Vučić used his constitutional powers to pardon 49 people, including 23 students and party loyalists suspected of offences related to what he called the "terrible events we have gone through over the past year and a half", according to Serbian public broadcaster RTS.

The upcoming parliamentary elections will pit Vučić's Progressive Party against a student-led, anti-corruption movement called Students Win and a coalition of pro-Western opposition parties known as European Serbia.

Vucic has been a fixture of Serbian politics for more than a decade , becoming prime minister in 2014, before being elected to his first term as president in 2017.

He has publicly said he wants Serbia to join the EU while courting close ties with Russia and opening Serbia up to Chinese investment.

articles.title: Israel revokes Dutch diplomats’ status over sanctions on settlements
articles.summary: Israel escalates retaliatory measures as Western sanctions target illegal West Bank settlements.
articles.body:
Israel has revoked the diplomatic status of Dutch diplomats at the Netherlands’ ‌Representative Office in Ramallah, Israel’s Foreign Ministry has said.

The countermeasure announced on Sunday comes in response to the Dutch government’s ban on ⁠imports originating ⁠from Israeli settlements in the ⁠occupied West Bank.

In a statement posted on X, Israel’s Foreign Minister Gidoen Saar said, “If the Netherlands wishes to continue representing its interests with the Palestinians, it may do so from Palestinian Authority territory, rather than from the territory of the State of Israel.”

Israel informed the Dutch embassy that “diplomats operating in Ramallah must return their Israeli-issued diplomatic documentation within seven days”.

Saar said, “Last month, we removed the Dutch delegation from the International Support Center for Gaza in Kiryat Gat, following actions taken by the Dutch Government against Israel. I reiterate: Israel will not ignore measures intended to harm it. Any country that acts in a hostile and unilateral manner against Israel will lose influence and relevance in the region.”

Israel has enacted a series of retaliatory measures in response to the United Kingdom, France and Canada announcing sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements.

Earlier this month, Israel announced a seven-day deadline for the removal of British representatives from the International Gaza Support Center as one of four countermeasures against the UK for imposing sanctions on illegal settlements in the West Bank.

The Netherlands brought its ban into force on September 22. The Dutch measure goes further than some others. It bans the import, purchase and sale of goods from illegal Israeli settlements, as well as services facilitating that trade.

Bilateral trade between the Netherlands and Israel totalled about $4.8bn last year. Its significance extends beyond the Dutch market, with the Netherlands serving as a major gateway for goods entering the rest of Europe.

The legal non-profit Global Echo group said the Netherlands accounted for a third of agricultural exports from Israel’s illegal settlements and nearly half of those destined for the European Union.

articles.title: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigns amid prolonged protests
articles.summary: Despite student-led protests and political unrest challenging his rule, Vucic intends to run in the snap elections.
articles.body:
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has resigned to seek the prime minister’s post in a snap parliamentary election on October 25, as a student-led movement mounts the most serious challenge to his rule in more than a decade.

Vucic, on the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) ballot, has dominated Serbian politics as president or prime minister since 2014. Barred from seeking a third presidential term, he is now seeking to extend his hold on power through the parliamentary vote.

Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabic, a close ally, will serve as acting president pending a presidential election. Vucic said one of his final acts in office was to pardon 49 people, including 23 convicted in connection with the protests.

Protests triggered by railway station disaster

The election follows nearly two years of demonstrations prompted by the killing of 16 people when a concrete canopy collapsed at a railway station in the northern city of Novi Sad on November 1, 2024.

Students have since organised some of Serbia’s largest demonstrations in decades, drawing hundreds of thousands of people onto the streets.

Protesters have accused the government of corruption, a lack of transparency and political interference in state institutions.

Vucic and his allies reject the allegations that they are responsible for the problems highlighted by the protesters.

The student movement is contesting the parliamentary election under the banner “Students Win”, with the backing of several opposition parties, including the Democratic Party, which was once led by former Serbian President Boris Tadic.

Its list of 250 candidates includes mostly university professors and professionals from a range of fields. Its platform calls for investigations into allegedly ill-gotten property, measures against corruption and political interference in public institutions and greater transparency in the use of public funds.

Some polls suggest that the student-backed movement could pose a serious threat to Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party, although the authenticity and methodology of some of the polls are difficult to independently verify.

Belgrade-based editor and columnist Dejan Ilic told Al Jazeera that Vucic should not be credited with choosing to hold an early election.

“Vucic is not the only actor in this country. People have said that Serbia is in a bad state, they demanded elections and they forced elections,” Ilic said.

‘The crisis could begin after the election’

Aida Corovic, a former Serbian parliamentarian and human rights activist, said the anger extended beyond the student movement.

“Serbia has been undergoing internal change in recent months,” Corovic told Al Jazeera.

“I fear that the crisis in Serbia could only begin after the October 25 elections,” she said. “This government has taken over the institutions, it is deeply intertwined with organised crime and it will try every possible way to remain in power.”

A few hours before his resignation, Vucic told CNN that if the opposition won, he would acknowledge the results and congratulate his opponents that same evening.

The political crisis in Serbia is being closely watched across the Western Balkans.

Belgrade maintains close political, economic and cultural ties with Serbian communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Kosovo, giving developments in Belgrade significant influence beyond its borders.

Tanja Topic, head of the Friedrich Ebert Foundation office in neighbouring Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina, said a change in Serbia’s political direction could ease tensions across the region.

“It is crucial that the paradigm in Serbia’s politics changes because it would bring relief to the entire region,” Topic told Al Jazeera.

She said Belgrade has for years sent mixed messages to its neighbours, presenting itself as a supporter of peace, stability and prosperity while, in her view, contributing to political tensions in the region.

That influence has been particularly significant in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Topic said, while relations between Serbia and Croatia have also deteriorated in recent years.

“We should not expect miracles overnight,” Topic remarked.

“Changing the value system would be a long and difficult process, but I think that disappointment if change does not come could have more serious and damaging consequences, both in Serbia and across the region.”

With a population of about six million, Serbia is the largest country in the Western Balkans with one of the region’s largest economies.

Vucic has promoted the country as an emerging economic success story, pointing to Chinese investment, energy supplies from Russia and, more recently, growing cooperation with Israel.

But average wages remain below those in neighbouring European Union member states.

According to official statistics, the average net monthly salary in Serbia was 1,032 euros ($1,174) in April, compared with 1,555 euros ($1,770) in neighbouring Croatia – a difference of about 51 percent compared with the EU member.

The contrast in living standards is one of several issues shaping public debate as voters prepare to return to the polls.

Serbia’s current political crisis is unfolding against the backdrop of the country’s unresolved wartime legacy.

More than two decades ago, NATO launched a bombing campaign against the then Federal Republic of Yugoslavia during the Kosovo war. At the time, Serbia was ruled by Slobodan Milosevic.

The legacy of the Balkans wars of the 1990s remains politically sensitive.

In early September, Ratko Mladic, the former commander of the Bosnian Serb army who was convicted by an international tribunal of genocide and war crimes committed during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, was buried in Belgrade.

His funeral, which was attended by several Serbian government ministers and included military honours, prompted international criticism.

The EU’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the bloc had no place for those who glorify war crimes.

The October election will therefore be watched not only as a contest over Serbia’s domestic political future, but also for what it may signal about the country’s direction and its relationship with the rest of the Western Balkans.

articles.title: ‘Atrocious’ crime: Cuban official decries possibility of US military action
articles.summary: Cuba’s deputy foreign minister slams US sanctions, labelling them ‘equivalent to genocide’.
articles.body:
A senior official in Cuba has warned that any prospective United States military action taken against the island nation would constitute a serious international crime, and has rejected claims made by US President Donald Trump that Cuba is a failed state.

On Sunday, Carlos Fernandez de Cossio, the country’s deputy foreign minister, told the US cable television channel C-SPAN’s flagship programme, Washington Journal, that it would be an “atrocious international crime for the US to use military force against Cuba, which is a peaceful neighbouring country”.

His comments come after Trump said during his Tuesday speech at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) that “freedom will be coming” to the island. His remarks prompted the Cuban delegation to exit the assembly hall. On Saturday, Trump brought up military action, telling reporters, “I don’t think we’ll need the military. Cuba is failing very badly.”

Fernandez de Cossio said that coercing nations who do not “submit” by disrupting their commercial shipments, attempting to handicap a population through starvation, depriving it of stable healthcare and withholding fuel, as the US has “done for nine months now”, is “equivalent to a genocide”.

The US has maintained a foreign policy of maximum economic pressure against Cuba for more than 60 years. The Trump administration has previously said that it wants a shake-up in Cuba’s government. Earlier this year, the administration enforced an additional oil and fuel blockade against the island, which has crippled the nation’s infrastructure, causing widespread fuel scarcity and rolling power outages. Government officials in Cuba cited systemic difficulties in securing food supplies and other basic necessities for the country of more than 10 million.

Fernandez de Cossio said Havana must ready its citizens for the prospect of US military aggression, adding that while Cuba recognises it might stand alone, it will still exercise its legitimate right to self-defence.

He explained that bilateral diplomatic channels with the US remain open but have yielded minimal results due to the economic stranglehold of ongoing sanctions, adding that Havana remains willing to engage with Washington in a “respectful manner” only if discussions accommodate mutual dignity, benefit both populations, and respect state sovereignty.

Several countries condemned the US’s continued economic sanctions and blockade of Cuba during the UNGA earlier this week.
